title: Estimating in points, in time, or by counting items; #NoEstimates in practice

videos.script: Every sprint, the Billing team sat down and gave each item a number. A one, a three, an eight. {{meeting}} Four months later, the files record two things side by side. What they guessed, and what happened. {{files}} So we can ask the uncomfortable question. Did the guess add anything to what the history already said? {{question}} In June, a one-point item took twelve days. A five-pointer took slightly less than a three. {{june}} In September the points looked better. Not because the guesses improved, but because the waiting had gone. {{september}} And counted week by week, the points were no steadier than simply counting items. {{counting}} This lesson compares the three ways of sizing work, and looks at the movement called NoEstimates. {{noestimates}} It ends with the four cases where an estimate really is worth what it costs. {{worth}}
